datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: TyDiQA-GoldP is natively collected by information-seeking speakers in each language. IndicQA is manually curated from Wikipedia articles on Indic topics. UDPOS uses natively-sourced Universal Dependencies treebank text. XLSum consists of BBC news articles natively authored in 44 languages. GLUECoS NLI uses Bollywood movie conversations. EN-ES-CS uses naturally occurring code-mixed tweets.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: XNLI: 'professional translations of the MNLI corpus into 14 languages'. Indic-XNLI: 'translates the XNLI dataset into 11 Indic languages by using Machine Translation'. PAWS-X: 'professionally translated from the PAWS dataset'. XCOPA: 'a translation of the COPA dataset into 11 typologically diverse languages'. XStoryCloze: 'translating the English StoryCloze dataset using professional translators'. MLQA: 'extractive QA dataset translated into 7 languages by professional translators'. XQuAD: 'professional translations of a subset of the SQuAD dataset'.

details.TyDiQA-GoldP: Natively collected information-seeking QA reflecting genuine needs of speakers in each language community.
details.IndicQA: Context paragraphs chosen from Wikipedia articles closely related to Indic culture, history, etc.
details.XLSum: BBC news articles natively authored for specific language communities by local journalists.
details.GLUECoS NLI: Bollywood movie conversations reflecting Indian bilingual cultural context.
details.EN-ES-CS: Naturally occurring English-Spanish code-mixed tweets from bilingual communities.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: MEGA aggregates 16 existing datasets; annotator profiles vary. TyDiQA-GoldP uses native speakers. XLSum uses native-language journalists. XNLI, PAWS-X, XCOPA, XStoryCloze, MLQA, XQuAD use professional translators (may or may not be native). WikiANN uses automatic annotation projection. Indic-XNLI uses MT with native speaker validation. The MEGA paper does not provide unified annotator information.

annotator_workforce.evidence: MEGA is an aggregation benchmark; the MEGA paper authors are from Microsoft Corporation, University of Washington, CMU, and JHU. Individual dataset annotator details are in the respective original papers, not in the MEGA paper.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: MEGA reveals significant English-centricity in multilingual LLM evaluation: (1) All prompt templates are written in English regardless of target language. (2) 7 of 16 datasets are translated from English sources. (3) GPT models show strong English performance bias with significant disparity for low-resource, non-Latin script languages. (4) Translate-test strategy (translating inputs to English) often improves performance, especially for low-resource languages, highlighting models' English-centric capabilities. (5) The paper notes 'there is a significant disparity between the performance of LLMs in English vs non-English languages'. (6) Even with possible test data contamination inflating scores, LLMs 'still vastly underperform on (especially low-resource) non-English languages'.

geographic_representation.primary_region: Global (but heavily Indo-European and South Asian)
notably_excluded: Most of Africa (limited to Swahili, Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Amharic, Oromo, Kirundi, Wolof, Nigerian Pidgin, Somali)
geographic_representation.evidence: MEGA encompasses 70 languages covering 21 different language families, with Indo-Aryan and Afro-Asiatic languages in the majority (Figure 1b). The paper acknowledges: 'there is very little representation from African languages, Indigenous languages of the Americas etc. in any of the evaluation benchmarks available today.'
